title: Argent worker protocol
description: Wire contract between the Argent workflow engine and external worker processes. Workers are provisioned by an administrator at POST-adjacent admin pages, which issue an API key shown exactly once; a client only ever presents that key. There is no client-side registration. All requests and responses are camelCase JSON; all values in parameter and output maps are strings.

identityResponse.description: What the presented key resolves to. Returned by GET /api/workers/me so a client can confirm its key at startup.

name.description: The worker name a WorkerActivity node targets.

runtime.description: What the client last reported about itself, for example "Argent Python Worker 0.1". Free-form: nothing routes on it. Null until the client first heartbeats.

heartbeatRequest.description: Liveness, and the only channel through which a client describes itself. A client provisioned by an administrator has no registration call, so this is where it says what it is.

runtime.description: Free-form identification, for example "Argent Python Worker 0.1". Deliberately not an enum. Overwrites the stored value; omit to leave it unchanged.

subjects.description: Subjects this client has handlers for. Overwrites the stored list; omit to leave it unchanged. Advertised for the admin worker list and not enforced, so a mismatch surfaces as a request that is never claimed.

concurrency.description: The cap the administrator set at provisioning. A claim is limited by it.

maxItems.description: Requested batch size. Clamped to the worker's configured concurrency, and the authenticated key — not this body — decides which worker is claiming.

task.description: One claimed unit of work. Claimed at most once at a time across all clients holding the same key.

id.description: Stable across delivery attempts. This is the idempotency key: a request redelivered after a lost lease carries the same id.

subject.description: Opaque task identifier chosen by the workflow author. The worker decides what it means.

parameters.description: Author-supplied key/value parameters. Values may have had {{variable}} placeholders interpolated from workflow variables.

timeoutSeconds.description: The author's hard budget. The request fails when it elapses even if the lease is still being renewed.

outputs.description: On success these become the token's process variables under the same keys, readable by later nodes and gateway conditions.

error.description: Required when succeeded is false. Surfaced to the workflow author in the node failure message.

leaseSeconds.description: Omit to take the server default of 60 seconds.
